One Staff, Two Readers
KHM 603 · Op. 48/2, movement I · viola · page 2, staff 4 · bars 22–26

One staff, as Zeus and the MuSViT reader receive it

The same viola staff, cut by compare.py exactly as both models are trained on it, then shrunk to each model's input height. Blue lines mark the units each model's attention works over: Zeus's 16-pixel columns and MuSViT's 16 × 16 patches. Bar 25, the 32nd-note broken chord both readers miss, is shown close up at the end.

The crop2,284 × 147 pxcut from the page rendered 2,800 px wide; the staff plus 2.5 spaces above and below
Zeus sees1488 × 96 px93 columns, each 16 px wide; a column's whole height becomes one step
MuSViT reader sees1984 × 128 px8 rows × 124 columns = 992 patches of 16 × 16 px

The staff as cut

Original crop 2,284 × 147 px, scaled to fit

Bars 22–23 are plain eighths and sixteenths, and both readers get them right. Bars 24–26 are where both go wrong: a grace note and 32nds in bar 24, then the broken-chord 32nds of bars 25 and 26.

What each reader receives

Zeus 96 px high · 16 px columns · actual size, scroll sideways
MuSViT reader 128 px high · 16 × 16 px patches · actual size, scroll sideways

Zeus's convolutions turn each 16-pixel column into one vector, the full height packed together; its decoder attends along that single row of 93 steps. MuSViT keeps the grid: its decoder attends over all 992 patches and has to work out vertical position, which is pitch, from which row a patch is in. Both read the whole staff at once and write the reading one symbol at a time.

Bar 25 up close

Original crop actual pixels
Zeus enlarged 5×: each blue strip is one step for its decoder
MuSViT reader enlarged 4×: each square is one patch

The crop is nine staff spaces high (the staff's four, and 2.5 above and below), so a staff space is about 11 px in Zeus's input and 14 px in the MuSViT reader's: a note on a line and one on the space beside it are 5 and 7 px apart. Each 32nd note gets about 21 px of width in Zeus's input, a little over one column, and about 28 px in the reader's, nearly two patch columns.

C4:32ndE4:32ndC4:32ndE4:32ndC4:32ndE4:32ndB2:16thE4:32ndE4:32ndA4:32ndE5:32ndG4:32ndE4:32ndG4:32ndG4:32nd bar wrong
MuSViT reader
C4:32ndE4:32ndG3:32ndE4:32ndC4:32ndE4:32ndF3:32ndE4:32ndC4:32ndE4:32ndA4:32ndE4:32ndC4:32ndE4:32ndF3:32ndC4:32nd bar wrong

Marked tokens differ from the encoding at that position. Zeus J drops two notes and loses the pattern partway through. The MuSViT reader (the larger-adapter model, trained without this movement) keeps all 16 notes and the rhythm but reads the low A3 as G3 or F3, a step or two low. The encoding's A4 at note 11 matches neither reader.
